title: Killed job is restarted by its scheduler

brief.headline: Continuity Guardian escalated
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 125369 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 28% over 30s (87/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,340/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 125369) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,340/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Waiting exceeds the 60s tolerated degradation ($132,511 revenue at risk vs 60s tolerated). Terminating carries a 2-minute replay cost but was previously ineffective (MEM-1). The blocker is a replayable, may_interrupt workload owned by pricing. No candidate action is viable without human owner decision.

audit.report: The batch_worker process for batch_replayable_price_sync became an idle-in-transaction blocker, causing checkout timeouts that dropped success rates to 55% and put approximately $13,340 per minute of revenue at risk. The business tolerance for degraded checkout is 60 seconds, but the expected remaining runtime of the workload (~596s) would far exceed this window, costing an estimated $132,511 in lost revenue if allowed to wait. Terminating the workload carries a 2-minute replay cost but avoids prolonged revenue loss; however, prior termination attempts were ineffective. The negotiation ultimately escalated to the pricing team owner for a human decision.
audit.root_cause: The batch_worker process for batch_replayable_price_sync entered an idle-in-transaction state, blocking checkout sessions and causing revenue-impacting timeouts.
lessons: Check idle-in-transaction blockers for batch_replayable_price_sync before they cascade into checkout timeouts; a 4-second idle window already signals risk.
Validate the replay cost and idempotency of batch_replayable_price_sync with the pricing owner before a failure, so termination vs. wait decisions can be made in under 2 minutes.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly identified that waiting exceeds the 60s tolerated degradation and that terminating carries a replay cost, but neither produced a viable candidate action within the 2-minute window, forcing escalation to the pricing owner.
follow_ups: Contact the pricing owner to confirm the replay procedure for batch_replayable_price_sync and whether a fresh termination would succeed where prior attempts failed.
Add a runtime monitor alert for batch_worker processes entering idle-in-transaction state on batch_replayable_price_sync to trigger a fast escalation before the 60s tolerance is breached.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync has been idle in transaction for 4.0s. The tradeoff probe is needed to quantify the cost of waiting versus interrupting, but the blocker appears active and not immediately harmful beyond the lock wait.
